notes: Liangzhu culture of the Yangtze delta (the brief asks for its start; the page's whole life, 3300-2300 BC, is drawn). The lead dates it '3300-2300 BC' and says it 'flourished around 2500 BC, but disappeared from the Taihu Lake area after around 2300 BC'; the page gives no phases. Type site at Liangzhu, Yuhang, Hangzhou; the walled city 'inner city covers 290 hectares', 'walled-area outside remains cover 700 hectares'. Extent: infobox 'Jiangsu, Shanghai, & Zhejiang in China'; the dossier draws the Songze (Lake Tai) country, the Hangzhou core and, because the Liangzhu page lists the Hemudu as a predecessor, the Ningbo plain (confidence 2; the page does not say the Liangzhu crossed Hangzhou Bay). Jade influence 'as far north as Shanxi' (Taosi) and 'as far south as Guangdong' is influence, not drawn. End: the page links the collapse to flooding ('between 4345 +- 32 years and 4324 +- 30 years B.P.') and the 4.2 kiloyear drought and names no successor, so the land goes to nobody in 2300 (the Maqiao culture follows in the archaeology but not on the page). The Dawenkou and Longshan are contemporaries, not neighbours on the page's map. No area figure.
